 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.
2. Brief case of the petitioner in the nutshell:

It is the case of the petitioners that, on 18.10.2018 at about 9.15 p.m, when the Sutapa Chakraborty (who herein after will be referred as deceased) was proceeding as a SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 pedestrian on White Field Road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations on the left side road and when she reached near Columbia Asia Hospital, White Field Road, Bengaluru at that time the rider of Dio scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JA- 4338 drove the scooter in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger the human life had dashed the deceased and caused the accident.
As a result of impact deceased fell on the road and sustained fatal injuries all over the body.
Though she was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital and thereafter she was shifted to Manipal Hospital and treated in the said Hospital as inpatient and she undergone several surgery.
Inspite of best treatment she died during the course of treatment on 22.10.2018.
It is stated that they have spent huge amount towards treatment of the deceased.
It is specifically contended that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.

It is contended that the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as tailor and earning Rs.350/-
per day and also getting monthly family pension of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter and as such the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the said vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.
Notice was duly served to respondent No.2, the respondent No.2 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.

sentences.text: After service of notice, respondent No.1 spurred in rush to the Court by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.1 admitting the issuance of insurance policy in respect of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JA-4338.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident.
Further contended that the insured vehicle is falsely implicated in the alleged accident.
Further it is contended that the complaint is lodged against un-known vehicle and there was a delay of 4 days in lodging FIR and this is fatal to the case of the petitioners.
Further negligence on the part of the rider of its insured vehicle is denied.
Per contra it is alleged that the unfortunate accident occurred on account of the sole negligence of the deceased without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the rider of the motorcycle did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.
Despite knowing the said fact the owner thereof had handed over its possession to such a driver.
On account of willful breach of the terms & conditions of the SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petitions.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that on 18.10.2018 at about 9.15 p.m, near Columbia Asia Hospital, White Field main road, Bengaluru, the rider of the Honda Dio motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JA-4338 rode it rash and negligently and dashed against the deceased by name Sutapa Chakraborty, who was walking on the left side of the road and caused her death ?
2) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. Petitioner No.2 examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 16 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
The Manager- Legal of respondent No.1 insurance company examined as RW.1 and Ex.R.1 & 2 got marked.
7. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.1 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per final order for the Bishal Chakraborty vs Tata Aig General Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95304764/
3  following :
 REASONS 9. ISSUE NO.1 : As this issue clinches the whole dispute in controversy, this issue is taken for discussion at the inception for better appreciation of evidence and dissection of materials placed on record.

sentences.text: The petitioners have knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation on account of death of one Sutapa Chakraborty in a Road Traffic Accident.
Before dwelling into analyzing the disputed facts in issue it is relevant to have the birds eye of the case of petitioners in a nutshell.

11. It is the case of the petitioners that, on 18.10.2018 at about 9.15 p.m, when the Sutapa Chakraborty (who herein after will be referred as deceased) was proceeding as a pedestrian on White Field Road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations on the left side road and when she reached near Columbia Asia Hospital, White Field Road, Bengaluru at that time the rider of Dio scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JA- 4338 drove the scooter in a rash and negligent manner so as to SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 endanger the human life had dashed the deceased and caused the accident.
As a result of impact deceased fell on the road and sustained fatal injuries all over the body.
Though she was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital and thereafter she was shifted to Manipal Hospital and treated in the said Hospital as inpatient and she undergone several surgery.
Inspite of best treatment she died during the course of treatment on 22.10.2018.
It is stated that they have spent huge amount towards treatment of the deceased.
It is specifically contended that postmortem was conducted and corpse was handed over to the family members.
It is contended that the deceased was hale and healthy and was working as tailor and earning Rs.350/- per day and also getting monthly family pension of Rs.25,000/- p.m.
It is further submitted that because of death of deceased the petitioners have suffered both financially and emotionally.

It is contended that the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the rider of scooter and as such the respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the owner of the said vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence prayed to allow the petition.

12. In order to substantiate the contentions of the petitioners, the petitioner No.2 stepped into the witness box and filed her affidavit-in-lieu of oral examination-in-chief as PW1 and got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P16 documents.

On the other hand in order to substantiate the defence of the respondent No.1 and SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 to demolish the case of the petitioners, the respondent No.1 counsel has cross examined PW.1 at length.
13. Repelling to the contentions urged by the petitioners, the respondent No.1 had attacked the case of the petitioners on various prisms known to fact and law.

The first and foremost contention urged by the respondent No.1 is that, the insured scooter was falsely implicated by colluding with the owner of the vehicle and jurisdictional police and there is inordinate delay of 4 days which is not explained by the petitioner.
Further denied all the allegations made in the petition.

Hence prayed to Bishal Chakraborty vs Tata Aig General Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95304764/
4 dismiss the petition.

sentences.text: 14. In support of these contentions the Manager - Legal of respondent No.1 company is examined as RW.1 and Ex.R.1 & 2 got marked.
In order to demolish the defence of the respondents and to substantiate the case of the petitioners, the petitioner's counsel has cross examined the RW.1 at length.

15. On marshaling of factual matrix, on dissection of evidence placed on record and after hearing on erudite counsel appearing for petitioner and respondent No.1, the moot questions arise for consideration are :
1) Whether petitioner in active collusion with police officials have falsely implicated the insured vehicle ?
SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 2) Whether the delay of 4 days in setting criminal law in motion is fatal for the case of the petitioners ?
16. With this prelude in the back drop let me unfurl each of the contentions urged by the combating parties and view the same in the beacon of light of documentary and oral evidence placed on record.

It is the specific contention of the respondent No.1 is that there is inordinate delay of 4 days in filing the FIS as such the petitioners in active collusion with respondent No.2 and police officials have falsely implicated the insured vehicle.
When this being the specific contention urged by the respondent No.1 it is relevant to fall back on the documentary and oral evidence placed before this court.
According to the version of the petitioners, the accident happened on 18.10.2018 at about 9.15 p.m.
The criminal law was set into motion on 22.10.2018 at about 8.30 a.m. there is approximately 4 days delay in filing the FIS.
It is relevant to note that Ex.P.2 was filed by the son of the petitioner.
The reasons for delay is also ventilated in Ex.P.2 itself stating that the deceased was badly injured in the accident.

From the date of accident till 22.10.2008 she was treated in various hospital and she breathed her last on 22.10.2018 as such the delay of four days is caused in setting criminal law into motion.
SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 17.
It is the specific case of the petitioners that, soon after the accident deceased was shifted to Columbia Asia Hospital and later shifted to Manipal Hospital for higher treatment.
Much was canvassed by learned counsel for the respondent No.1 that, no CCTV footage had taken at the spot.
The CCTV Footage will become the relevant when there is a stout denial with regard to the involvement of the vehicle.
In the instant case on hand having regard to the statement of the eyewitnesses and accused as per Ex.P.10 to 12 it reflects that there is a involvement of the Insured vehicle.
It is the respondent No.1 who had disputed the involvement of the vehicle.
Respondent No1 had not made endeavor to summon the IO.
The petitioners have mainly relied on chargesheet which also includes the statement of the eye-witness and also the statement of the rider of the two wheeler.

sentences.text: It is the respondent No.1 who has grievance as against the chargesheet.

When such being the case,
the onus shifts on respondent No.1 to disprove the contents of the chargesheet.
The respondent No.1 did not made any endevour to summon the IO in disproving the charge- sheet.
18. The main anchorage of the case of the respondent No.1 is based on Ex.P.4 IMV Report wherein there is no mention about the damages to the vehicle.
It is needles to mention that criminal law was set into motion after 4 days from the date of accident.
The vehicle was inspected on 23.10.2018 which SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 means to say there is already 6 days have been elapsed from the date of accident.
When such is the case there are every chances of respondent No.2 getting repaired his vehicle as such the damages were not visible in the vehicle.
Only for the reasons that, Ex.P.4 reflects that there is no damages to the vehicle that itself does not falsify the case of the petitioners herein.
19. Much was attacked stating that there was no CCTV footage.

If there was the CCTV footage as alleged by respondent No.1 then the question is arise in the mind of this court as to what prevented the respondent No.1 to produce the the said CCTV footage of the relevant time.
Another important aspect to be noted herein is the rider of the offending bike has given statement admitting his guilt as per Ex.P.10.
Further more it is not the case of respondent No.1 that, respondent No.2 and petitioner are colluded each other with an malafide intention to wangle the compensation amount.
20. The next aspect to be considered is with regard to the delay.
The reasons for delay is ventilated in Ex.P2 complaint itself.
When the deceased is fighting for her life, the relatives of the deceased cannot be expected to set criminal law in motion.
The predominant responsibility of the family of the deceased will be saving the kith and kin's life rather fighting for justice.
When such being the case this court cannot found fault with the mere SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 delay of 4 days in lodging FIR.

In this regard it is relevant to relay on the decision reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, in the case of Ravi v/s Bhadrinarayana and others, wherein it is held that "It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station''.
"The purpose of lodging the FIR in motor accident cases is primarily to intimate the police to initiate investigation of criminal offences.
Lodging of FIR certainly proves factum of accident so that the victim is able to lodge a case for compensation but delay in doing so cannot be the main ground for rejecting the claim petition.

In other words, although lodging of FIR is vital in deciding motor accident claim cases, delay in lodging the same should not be treated as fatal for such proceedings, if claimant has been able to demonstrate satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
Unless kith and kin of the victim are able to regain a certain level of tranquillity of mind and are composed to lodge it, even if there is delay, the same deserve to be condoned.

In such circumstances, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 Bishal Chakraborty vs Tata Aig General Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95304764/
6 more significance than delay in lodging thereof supported by cogent reasons.

entities.text: SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 Bishal Chakraborty vs Tata Aig General Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: If the court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground."
(Emphasis supplied by me)
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The principles reiterated in the above decision squarely applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The ratio decidendi laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The petitioner had explained the SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 delay caused.
The petitioners have clearly demonstrated as to the involvement of the insured vehicle in the accident.

21. The learned counsel for the respondent.no.1 as a last row to the sinking boat, for the contentions urged has contended that, Fraud and Justice never dwell together and also urged that there is a toxic nexus between the claimants, police officials and insured.
The said contention will not hold any water in the eye of law.
The said contention would have gain weightage if respondent no.1 would have proved the toxic nexus between the claimants and police authorities.
In the absence of such solely on the basis of assumptions, presumptions, speculations, the version of Respondent No.1 cannot be trusted as a gospel truth.
22. The next aspect to be analysed is with regard to factum of negligence.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.

These elements are as follows:
Duty:
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
Here it is important to understand whether the defendant has taken legal duty of care towards the plaintiff.
SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 Breach of Duty
: After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
It talks about the breach of duty on the part of the defendant which he/ she is expected to do as he/ she has some legal duty towards the plaintiff.
The action of causing something: It means that the damage caused to the plaintiff is due to the act of the defendant.
Here the defendant may do an act which is not expected from him/her or the defendant may be negligent in not doing an act which was expected from him/ her.

sentences.text: Damages:
At last what matters is, there must be some damage/injury that is caused to the plaintiff and this damages should be the direct consequence of the defendant's act.

Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
Reverting back to the factual matrix Ex.P.1 FIR as its germane in Ex.P.2 FIS.
It is interesting to note that no doubt the FIR was lodged belatedly.
But the delay is properly explained.

Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.1 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioners after the accident.

24. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car.

The view taken by this Court that the police records are prima- facie proof in support of the case of the petitioner, is supported by the decision rendered in Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others reported in 2013 (4) T.A.C 5 (S.C.), wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held thus:
In view of the aforesaid facts, the Tribunal should have considered both oral and documentary evidence referred to supra and appreciated the same in the SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 proper perspective and recorded the finding on the contentious issue No. 1 & 2 in the affirmative.

The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.

The registration of FIR and filing of the charge-sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.

It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others reported in (2009) 13 SCC 530 has observed that, it is necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.

sentences.text: The claimants are merely required to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied.

Further the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Krishnappa and another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105,
where the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka considering the fact that the rider of the offending vehicle was not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scooterist held that the accident had occurred due to rash or negligent driving by the rider of the offending van.

sentences.text: Even in the instant case the rider of the scooter is not examined to show that there was no negligence on his part and even otherwise the IO, as already observed, has clearly SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 opined that the accident occurred only due to the fault of the driver of the car and he was charge sheeted.
26. The petitioners in order to prove the factum of negligence has mainly relied on Ex.P.3 Spot mahazar.

On careful perusal of Spot mahazar it reflects that the deceased was proceeding as pedestrian was hit by the offending vehicle itself clearly shows that there is a negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
Added more Ex.P.7 chargesheet was also filed as against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Though PW.1 cross examined at length by respondent counsel but nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of cross examination.
But having regard to spot mahazar and other materials placed on record it is clearly forthcoming that shear negligence on the part of the rider of the vehicle.
As such this court cannot found fault with the version of the petitioner herein.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the scooter.
On assessing entire evidence the light of oral and documentary proof, the preponderance of probability tilts infavour of petitioners herein.
Hence, this tribunal answers the issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
27. ISSUE NO.2:
The petitioners claim that, Petitioner.No.1 is the son and petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
To prove the same, petitioner No.2 filed affidavit SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed about the above relationship.
The Aadhar cards marked at Ex's.P.13 & 14 and contents of the police papers do fortify the said fact.
It is pertinent to note that this relationship of the petitioners with the deceased has not been disputed by the respondents.

Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.

sentences.text: In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that, deceased was working as tailor and earning Rs.350/- per day and also she getting monthly family pension of Rs.25,000/-p.m.
To prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents to show that the deceased was working as tailor and earning of Rs.350/-per day.
29. Be that as it may, in the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2018.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
30. The next moot question to be considered is as to how the notional income has to be considered in the eye of law.

It is relevant to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 18.10.2018.
Therefore, Rs.12,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
31. The petitioners have produced the Aadhar card to show the age of the deceased as per Ex.P13.

The contents ingrained in the Aadhar card of the deceased discloses the date of date of birth as 18.11.1958 and the accident had taken place on 18.10.2018 and it shows that, at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 59 years.

Hence the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is '9'.
32.

As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

sentences.text: The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and she died at the age of 59 years.
Therefore, in this case, 10% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 59 years and as such, 10% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.13,750/- p.m. (Rs.12,500/-
+ 1,250/- i.e. 10%).
SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 33.
The deceased died living behind 2 dependents.

As per principle laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sarala Verma Case, 1/3rd of his income is required to be deducted towards his personal expenses which comes to Rs.9,167/- p.m. (Rs.13,750 - Rs.4,583 = Rs.9,167/-).
34. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.9,167/- p.m. and the multiplier '9' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.9,90,036/- (Rs.9,167 X 12 X 9).
Considering the above facts, this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.9,90,000/- under the head of loss of dependency.

35. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.16,500/- towards loss to estate and Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.
36. In this case, the petitioner No.1 and 2 are the son and daughter of the deceased and

as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents and children to get compensation in the case of an accidental death of a children and father as the case may be.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a father cause great shock and agony to the children of the deceased and she lost her love and affection towards his/her mother.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 & 2 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each under the head of Filial consortium.
37. MEDICAL EXPENSES :
Medical bill produced by PW.1 is marked at Ex.P16.
As per that, the claimants have spent Rs.80,857/- towards medical expenses of the deceased.
On close perusal of bill issued by Manipal Hospital wherein it is clearly mentioned as "Ins.Comp.name : National Insurance Company Limited".
During the course of cross examination PW.1 categorically admitted that 'It is true to suggest that bills at Ex.P.16 are reimbursed by National Insurance Company to the extent of Rs.2,12,619/-.
It is true to suggest that we only paid Rs.80,857/- out of the said bill from our own pocket'.
Hence the said words clearly discloses that the Manipal Hospital bill was paid by National Insurance Insurance Company.
Further on close perusal of document dated 22.10.2018 it reflects that National Insurance Co.Ltd paid Rs.2,12,619/- and a sum of Rs.80,857/- was paid by patient.
There is no contra evidence to disbelieve the genuineness of this bills.
Hence a sum of SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 Rs.80,857/- which is rounded off to Rs.81,000/- is awarded under this head.

Though the insurance company contended that the insured has violated the terms and conditions of the policy, no evidence is adduced to prove such breach of terms and conditions of the policy by the second respondent.

ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners proves that on 18.10.2018 at about 9.15 p.m, near Columbia Asia Hospital, White Field main road, Bengaluru, the rider of the Honda Dio motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-JA-4338 rode it rash and negligently and dashed against the deceased by name Sutapa Chakraborty, who was walking on the left side of the road and caused her death ?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In the instant case on hand having regard to the statement of the eyewitnesses and accused as per Ex.P.10 to 12 it reflects that there is a involvement of the Insured vehicle.
It is the respondent No.1 who had disputed the involvement of the vehicle.
Respondent No1 had not made endeavor to summon the IO.
Bishal Chakraborty vs Tata Aig General Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95304764/
5
When such being the case,
the onus shifts on respondent No.1 to disprove the contents of the chargesheet.
When such is the case there are every chances of respondent No.2 getting repaired his vehicle as such the damages were not visible in the vehicle.
Only for the reasons that, Ex.P.4 reflects that there is no damages to the vehicle that itself does not falsify the case of the petitioners herein.
The reasons for delay is ventilated in Ex.P2 complaint itself.
When the deceased is fighting for her life, the relatives of the deceased cannot be expected to set criminal law in motion.
The predominant responsibility of the family of the deceased will be saving the kith and kin's life rather fighting for justice.
When such being the case this court cannot found fault with the mere SCCH-23 MVC.1478/2019 delay of 4 days in lodging FIR.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus, cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.
If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
In the absence of such solely on the basis of assumptions, presumptions, speculations, the version of Respondent No.1 cannot be trusted as a gospel truth.
Before dwelling into analyzing the factum of alleged negligence it is relevant to have the conceptual aspects pertaining to factum of negligence.
There are four basic elements that a person has to fulfill in order to do a negligent act.
For committing a negligent act, there must be some duty on the part of the defendant.
: After fulfilling the first criteria the plaintiff must prove that the defendant has breached the legal duty imposed on him/her.
Bishal Chakraborty vs Tata Aig General Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95304764/
7
Negligence means a breach of duty caused by omission to do something which has reasonable man guide by those consideration which ordinarily regulated conduct of human affairs would do which a prudent man would not do.
In common prevalence negligence connoted to the want of proper care and the rashness conveys the idea of recklessness or the doing of an act without due consideration.
Moreover where the standard of proof required is preponderance of probabilities and the facts before the court probablizes the reasons assigned by PW.1 for delaying the lodging of the FIR as such this court cannot uphold the contention of the respondent No.1 regarding the delay by considering the condition of the petitioners after the accident.
24. Wherefore in the absence of any cogent evidence which could rebut the assertions made by PW-1 on oath supported by Ex.P-7 which is the charge sheet and the documents annexed therewith, this court should not have any impediment to conclude that the said documents prima-facie suffice to hold that accident, occurred due to rash and actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the car.
But it has recorded the finding in the negative on the above issues by adverting to certain statements of evidence of AW-1 and referring to certain alleged discrepancies in the FIR without appreciating entire evidence of AW- 1 and AW-2 on record properly and also not assigned valid reasons in not accepting their testimony.
The Tribunal should have taken into consideration the pleadings of the parties and legal evidence on record in its entirety and held that the accident took place on 19.07.1992, due to which Tikaram sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the same and the case was registered by the Uniara Police Station under Sections 279 and 304-A, IPC read with Sections 133 and 181 of the M.V. Act against the first and second respondents.
The registration of FIR and filing of the charge-sheet against respondent Nos.1 & 2 are not in dispute, therefore, the Tribunal should have no option but to accept the entire evidence on record and recorded the finding on the contentious issue Nos.1 and 2 in favour of the appellants.
Bishal Chakraborty vs Tata Aig General Ins Co Ltd on 13 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95304764/
8
It is necessary to reassert that in a claim for compensation filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, the claimant is expected to prove the incident on basis of principle of preponderance of probabilities and the view taken by this Court is fortified by the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Kusum and others V/s Satbir and others which is reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.
On careful perusal of Spot mahazar it reflects that the deceased was proceeding as pedestrian was hit by the offending vehicle itself clearly shows that there is a negligence on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle.
But having regard to spot mahazar and other materials placed on record it is clearly forthcoming that shear negligence on the part of the rider of the vehicle.
Consequently this tribunal hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the rider of the scooter.
Since the evidence led by the petitioners is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, this Tribunal hold that the petitioners are the legal representative of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioners are the legal heir and dependents of deceased.

9 28.
Therefore, Rs.12,500/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.
